newsitem.title: RUSSIA: FORECAST-Russia c.bank sees 10-12 pct CPI in 1997.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Russia c.bank sees 10-12 pct CPI in 1997.

text.p: Russian central bank policy is aiming for an inflation rate of 10 to 12 percent next year, First Deputy Chairman Alexander Khandruyev said on Wednesday.

"In the central bank's estimation, the average monthly inflation rate in the first 10 months of this year was 1.7 percent compared with 7.5 percent last year," Khandruyev told a conference on foreign investment in Russia.
He said that if such rates were maintained, the targets agreed for the year by the government and central bank would be met.
"For 1997, all central bank monetary policy is oriented towards inflation of 10-12 percent a year," he said.
Russia has slashed inflation from a monthly high of 17.8 percent in January 1995 to 0.3 percent last month. The government has forecast inflation of 1.2 percent in October.
Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin said earlier this month annual inflation should fall to 10 percent in 1997.
Khandruyev said improvements to the macro-economic situation would help boost foreign investment.
"It is quite clear that we must continue the monetary policy geared at bringing down the rate of inflation," he said, adding the exchange rate must be such as to depress inflationary expectations.
"The rate of growth of the dollar to the rouble must be lower than the average rate of inflation," he said.
The rouble is held in a declining corridor against the dollar providing for a gradual devaluation against the U.S. currency.
